page: p. 50 (leaf n69), Table of Seven Graffiti of Philae, rows A and C; described p. 33 (leaf n52)
object: graffito, two lines, neatly executed (39 x 6 cm)
site: Philae, Great Temple (Isis), East Colonnade, doorway just south of the Temple of Imuthes, west face of the north jamb, about 7.5 ft above the pavement
notes: Griffith prints the text only in his comparative table of seven Philae adoration graffiti (95, 96, 121-125), split by phrase: row A gives stone l. 1, row C l. 2 (marked 'end'); rows B, D, E have nothing for 95. Squeeze Borchardt, photo Berlin Academy 471, original compared January 1910. p. 33: 'The second letter of the last group, l, is quite clear, but is cut in a fault in the stone'; meaning perhaps 'The obeisance made on behalf of (?) the envoy remaineth (?) before Isis in Philae' (p. 51: 'The adoration made by (?) the envoy piously (?) before Isis in Philae'). tewisti = Eg. demotic t-wste, 'obeisance'; apote 'envoy'; pileqetel 'in Philae'. The group yeSo is o + the closed s-sign, not q (checked at 2.5x against the q of pileqetel).
